9.11.3. qnav.util.system

9.11.3.1. common.py

summary:

Provides commonly used project functions. This module contains commonly used (non-calculation) functions that are called throughout the project. These are namely for providing information about the project and the current platform.

author:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First full implementation of module

qnav.util.system.get_toolbox_version() → str[source]

A simple function to return the current version number of the toolbox. This is useful for reporting information that may dependent on the build of the software, such as generated results or reported errors.

Returns:

The decimal version number for the toolbox.

Return type:

str

qnav.util.system.get_system_name(return_min: bool = False) → str[source]

Return a short string for identifying the host operating system. This is namely used for identifying the operating system in a human-readable format. This is useful for identifying the type of system used when running an experiment.

Parameters:

return_min (bool) – If set to true, only the operating system name and major version number will be returned.

Returns:

A short string used for identifying the host operating system.

Return type:

str

qnav.util.system.get_platform_details() → str[source]

A simple function that returns a description of the platform. This function returns a string including the python version, processor platform architecture of the host system.

Returns:

A string describing the platform.

Return type:

str

qnav.util.system.is_window_platform() → bool[source]

A simple function which will return true if the system’s operating system is Microsoft Windows based. Otherwise, this function will return false.

Returns:

Returns true if the host operating system is Windows based.

Return type:

bool

qnav.util.system.is_mac_platform() → bool[source]

A simple function which will return true if the system’s operating system is Mac-OS based. Otherwise, this function will return false.

Returns:

Returns true if the host operating system is Mac-OS based.

Return type:

bool

qnav.util.system.is_linux_platform() → bool[source]

A simple function which will return true if the system’s operating system is Linux/Unix based. Otherwise, this function will return false.

Returns:

Returns true if the host operating system is Linux based.

Return type:

bool
